\section{Introduction}
The notions of observables and states are fundamental to mechanics. In this entry, we shall begin with the conceptual background to these ideas, then proceed to examine how these notions work in classical, statistical, and quantum mechanics.
The basis for these notions lies in making numerical measurements on physical systems and comparing the observed values with predicted theoretical values. The value measured will depend on the quantity being measured and upon the initial and boundary conditions imposed on the system. To account for this dependence, we introduce observables and states --- an observable is a mathematical entity in a theory which represents a measurement which can be made on the physical system described by that theory and a state is a mathematical entity which encodes conditions placed on that system.
